subject: Cloud Computing
title: How Your Data Reaches the Cloud
description: Learn How Your Data Reaches the Cloud in one minute.

hook.text: You click 'save' and your file appears in the cloud. But it actually traveled thousands of miles.

buildup.text: Data leaves your device, hits your router, travels to your ISP, then crosses fiber-optic backbone networks.

discovery.text: Cloud providers build private backbone networks connecting their data centers at the speed of light.

twist.text: Most of your internet traffic never touches the 'public' internet. It rides on private fiber.

climax.text: Google alone operates over 100,000 miles of private undersea and land fiber-optic cable.

punchline.text: The cloud feels instant. The fiber underneath makes it so.

quiz.question: How do major cloud providers connect their global data centers?
options: Through private fiber-optic backbone networks they own and operate
Exclusively through the public internet like everyone else
Using satellite connections for all inter-datacenter traffic

details.summary: Data travels from your device through local networks, ISP infrastructure, internet exchange points, and high-speed backbone networks before reaching a cloud data center. Cloud providers also maintain private backbone networks that bypass the public internet for faster, more reliable connections.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the network path to the cloud explains latency, reliability, and why region selection matters. The physical distance data travels directly affects application performance.
takeaways: Data traverses multiple networks between you and the cloud
Cloud providers maintain private backbone networks globally
Internet exchange points connect different networks efficiently

faq.question: How fast does data travel to the cloud?
faq.answer: Light in fiber travels at about 200,000 kilometers per second. A round trip from New York to a Virginia data center takes about 10 milliseconds. Cross-country to Oregon takes 60 to 80 milliseconds. Across the Atlantic to Europe takes 80 to 120 milliseconds.

faq.question: What are cloud provider backbone networks?
faq.answer: Google, AWS, and Microsoft operate private fiber optic networks spanning continents and oceans. Once your data enters their network at the nearest point of presence, it travels on their private backbone rather than the public internet, providing lower latency and higher reliability.
